basis: Lysosomal lipid storage with liver injury; intestinal infiltration causes steatorrhea (80-99% in supplied HPO). Cognitive damage is not characteristic across LAL subtypes.
Defined by intellectual disability, congenital myopathy and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; myopia and ptosis reported in 80-99%.
Inflammation of maxillary sinus mucosa; sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis. An infectious or autoimmune cause is not specified.
Myeloid neoplasm arising in marrow and blood, with splenic involvement within the same axis.
Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction disorder; weakness and ptosis reflect impaired transmission, without independent muscle or eye damage.
Severe combined immunodeficiency defined by defective T-cell development/function; organ-specific infectious manifestations are reported in only 5-29%.
Defined by olivopontocerebellar degeneration and sensorineural deafness; nystagmus is neurologic, while destructive ocular abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Intellectual disability and global developmental delay in 5/5; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage; joint and healing findings occur in 1/4.
Congenital contractures and mandibular hypoplasia define skeletal and joint involvement; nipple abnormalities have no axis.
Infertility due to uterine disease is confined to reproductive organs outside the thirteen axes.
Brittle sulfur-deficient hair defines the umbrella disorder; supplied neurologic, ocular and skeletal manifestations are each only 5-29%.
Hereditary corticospinal tract degeneration; weakness and amyotrophy are neurogenic. Urinary symptoms are uncommon and do not establish urinary-organ injury.
Benign peripheral nerve sheath neoplasm with epithelioid morphology; a cutaneous origin is not specified.
Squamous carcinoma originating in the esophagus; local growth does not establish common involvement of another organ axis.
Autoimmunity defines this heterogeneous umbrella; ear, airway, salivary and ocular sites vary among subtypes, with no single anatomical axis shared by most.
SCID with defining exfoliative dermatitis, alopecia and inflammatory enteropathy/chronic diarrhea; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish liver injury.
Whipworm infection occupies and injures intestinal mucosa; clinically significant blood-loss anemia occurs mainly with heavy infection.
Myofibroblastic neoplasm originating in the bladder; its inflammatory infiltrate does not make it an autoimmune or infectious disease.
Primary phalangeal osteolysis and sclerosis; associated redness and swelling do not establish a separate skin disorder.
Immune-mediated systemic inflammatory lymphoproliferative disease; renal injury varies by subtype and is not securely established above 30% across this umbrella.
Platelet defect and immunodeficiency; chronic eczema/skin inflammation common (rash 3/3), colitis 1/3. Vasculitis also reported (1/3), omitted under four-axis cap.
Cerebellar malformation; septo-optic dysplasia reported in 30-79% supports optic-nerve involvement. Other ocular, renal and cardiac anomalies are only 5-29%.
Neurologic startle disorder with hypertonia; no independent organ damage is established.
Umbrella metabolic disorder defined by abnormal glucose regulation; complications of particular subtypes do not apply across the group.
Corticomeningeal vascular disease with progressive cerebral injury; hemianopia is central. Marbled skin and telangiectases alone do not establish skin damage.
